questions.q: What does RTO (Recovery Time Objective) actually measure?
options: How many backups a policy must retain
How much data can be lost during a restore
How long a system can be down before that downtime becomes unacceptable
The exact cost of a cloud outage in dollars
questions.explain: RTO is a time budget for downtime — how long an outage can last before it's genuinely unacceptable to the business.

questions.q: What does RPO (Recovery Point Objective) actually measure?
options: How many Availability Zones a deployment must span
How much data loss, measured in time, is acceptable if restoring from a backup
The maximum size of a single backup file
How long a restore operation is allowed to take
questions.explain: RPO is about acceptable data loss, expressed as a time window since the last good backup — not about downtime.

questions.q: A business sets an RPO of 1 hour for an order-processing system. What does that require from the backup schedule?
options: Backups only need to run once a week
Backups must run at least every 60 minutes, with no exceptions
No backups are needed if the system has high availability
A single nightly backup is sufficient, as long as it never fails
questions.explain: An RPO of 1 hour structurally rules out anything less frequent than hourly backups, since the worst-case loss must stay within 1 hour.

questions.q: According to this lesson, in what order should RTO/RPO and the backup schedule be decided?
options: There is no real relationship between the two
The backup schedule is picked first based on convenience, then RTO/RPO are calculated from it
RTO and RPO only matter after a disaster has already happened
RTO and RPO are set first, as business decisions, and the backup schedule is built to satisfy them
questions.explain: Picking a schedule first and calling it a strategy has the order backwards — the objectives should drive the schedule, not follow from it.

questions.q: Why might a system have a tight RTO but a loose RPO (or vice versa)?
options: Because RTO and RPO measure different kinds of failure impact and can differ independently for the same workload
Because only one of the two numbers is ever relevant to a given system
Because RTO and RPO always have to be set to the exact same value
Because RPO only applies to databases and RTO only applies to web servers
questions.explain: A static marketing site might need fast recovery (tight RTO) but tolerate losing a day of edits (loose RPO); a quiet batch job might tolerate slow recovery but demand near-zero data loss for financial records.
